summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.25/1252)

data.turoyo: Yaʕni u ḥa d mafṭarwo, nəquṣo d luwewo ḏərura mə toxtor, rapor mede, nošo l uxalwo. U ʕamo kule ṣamwo. Nošo dlo ṣawmo luwewo.
data.translation: That is, the one who broke the fast, unless there was a necessity from a doctor, a report or something, no one would eat. All the people used to fast. There would be no one without fasting.

rationale: First Infectum-wa III.1 example; retains the medical-exception qualification and the edition-free supplied wording without asserting a lexical disobedience meaning. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.4/836)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Qamayto mašəġinawo iḏoṯayna w foṯayna. Mafṭərinawo w əzzanowo lu šuġlo. Kule šuġlo.
data.translation: Father Brahim: First we used to wash our hands and faces. We used to have breakfast and go to work. Always work.

rationale: First Infectum-wa III.2 example; unambiguous habitual breakfast before work. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

data.turoyo: Ṣafro, i saʕa šwaʕ w falge, bəṯr me d ḥləqli w mašəġli foṯi, mafṭallan ʕam ḥḏoḏe, dawšo, zəbdo, čay, laḥmo w gweto.
data.translation: Morgens um halb acht, nachdem ich mich rasiert und mein Gesicht gewaschen hatte, frühstückten wir zusammen: Honig, Butter, Tee, Brot und Käse.

rationale: Thin Preterit sense-2 cell; first-person plural actor, comitative and standalone menu context.

data.turoyo: Haṯe ʕanʕana yo gabayye, me meqəm mo (100) əšne gabayye, laǧan d qaymi b lalyo lu Ramaḏan. D mafṭəri, hala d saymi u ṣəḥuraṯṯe, laǧan d ṣaymi.
data.translation: This is a tradition among them; it has been among them since a hundred years ago, so that they get up at night for Ramadan, to have breakfast, or rather to have their pre-dawn meal, so that they fast.

rationale: Thin Infectum III.2 cell; retain the speaker’s explicit hala correction from breakfast to suhur. Night-before-fasting context must not be recoded as evening fast-breaking. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

data.turoyo: Ṣafro qayəm omər: "Qum, abri, qum əzzano mafṭərina, mṣalena w əzzan lu šuġlayḏan!"
data.translation: In the morning he rose, he says, 'Get up, my son, get up, let us go and have breakfast, pray, and go to our work!'

rationale: Thin Infectum III.2 cell; first-person plural invitation rather than another new Imperativ box. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

before: das Fasten brechen, nachdem das Fasten vorbei ist;
after: das Fasten brechen, das Fasten beenden;
rationale: Jan 1.25/1252 invokes a medical necessity/report as an exception to communal fasting. The inherited restriction nachdem das Fasten vorbei ist is too narrow. Keep one fast-ending sense; the exact timing and whether this is exemption versus interruption remain questions.

summary: All five records match the inherited two senses: breakfast in 9/25–26, 10/10 and 69/363, and breaking a religious fast in 94/46. No new sense or fixed collocation is established.
Stem III breakfast has an l-series Preterit agent without a governed patient. The list of foods in 10/10 specifies the meal; it does not by itself prove transitivity.
The mafṭall- Preterit and mafṭann- Infectum shapes reflect assimilation; the source’s maftanno/ftorayḏi t spelling is retained as a textual variant rather than silently changed to ṭ.
ftorayḏi is a possessed meal noun already filed under Infinitiv in the inherited entry. Preserve that filing and distinguish it from a finite clause.

Round 2 only. Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is project machine translation [MT]; readings rest on the supplied Turoyo. Existing and round-1 wording and numbering are retained. No edition translation is inferred.
The new Infectum-wa box has two established senses: habitual breakfast and ending/interruption of a religious fast. A medical reason is a contextual circumstance, not a new valency frame.
All Jan forms remain stem III. Hortative mafṭərina is Infectum, not Imperativ; neither a meal object nor a Detransitive is present.
The inherited meal noun under Infinitiv remains as round 1 treated it. No new idiom or meal-name sense is introduced.
Confirm source t versus inherited ṭ in 9/25–26 against the edition; no source-normalizing fix is proposed.

At Jan 1.25/1252, does mafṭarwo denote exemption before fasting, eating during the fast, or its eventual completion? Explain nəquṣo d. The gloss is neutral about timing and does not label the person a violator.
Jan examples have project machine translations [MT], not edition translations. Editors should check these English renderings against the Turoyo before treating them as vetted translations.
Ramadan context alone does not select fast-ending sense 1: mafṭəri is explicitly corrected to pre-dawn suhur before the fast begins.
